rules.sentence: Brugada syndrome vs arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
Typical symptoms	Syncope, cardiac arrest Especially nocturnal
ECG repolarization	Right precordial ST elevation and TWI
ECG depolarization	RBBB/LAD
AV conduction times	Prolonged PR/HV interval
Variability of ECG changes	Dynamic
Imaging	Normal (or mild RVOT dilatation)
Biopsy	Normal
Ventricular arrhythmias	Polymorphic VT, VF
Mechanism of VT	Phase 2 re-entry or local micro-reentry
Programmed ventricular stimulation	Inducibility of VF
Natural history	Sudden death
Brugada syndrome vs arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
Typical symptoms	Palpitations, syncope, cardiac arrest
ECG repolarization	Right precordial TWI
ECG depolarization	Right precordial QRS prolongation, ε waves
AV conduction times	Normal
Variability of ECG changes	Fixed
Imaging	Structural RV (and LV) abnormalities with global and regional dilation and dysfunction
Biopsy	Fibrofatty replacement
Ventricular arrhythmias	Monomorphic VT, VF
Mechanism of VT	Scar-related macro-reentry
Programmed ventricular stimulation	Inducibility of monomorphic VT or VF
Natural history	Sudden death, heart failure
